title: Check yourself: where the server's security steps go

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A server's chain has a participant P ahead of VerifyMac. Someone without the terminal's key sends a request with a made-up MAC, and VerifyMac votes ABORTED. For which P does the made-up request still leave an effect behind?

options.text: A P that reserves the amount in prepare and releases it in abort, since the reservation came before the vote
options.says: a joined participant is called on the abort path, so its abort releases the reservation; the abort undoes it

options.text: A P that forwards the request to the network with QueryHost in prepare, since the network acts before the vote
options.says: QueryHost sends in prepare and does not join; the network approves, and the abort can't take that back

options.text: A P that writes the request to a journal in its commit, since a journal entry outlives the transaction
options.says: commit is never called on an aborted transaction, so nothing is written

options.text: A P that puts the destination's name in the Context in prepare, since the Context is kept after the vote
options.says: what is in the Context never leaves our server; nothing outside acted on the request

origin.section: 7.2 A Request's MAC Is Checked Before Anything Acts on It

questions.stem: A production q2.log is attached to a support ticket, and the ticket system is breached. The SMAdaptor and KeyStoreAdaptor were deployed with logger="Q2" behind a ProtectedLogListener that protects 2, 35 and 45. The LMK file and the key file were not taken. What does the log give the attacker?

options.text: The card numbers of the requests the module MACed, since the MAC input is logged as hex that no listener masks
options.says: the Generate CBC-MAC entry holds the packed request in hex; a byte array isn't a message, so ProtectedLogListener leaves it

options.text: The PINs of the purchases the module translated, since each block is logged next to the key it is under
options.says: the key in the log is under the LMK; without dev.lmk the block can't be read

options.text: Nothing about the cards, since the log listener masks the card fields wherever they appear
options.says: it masks fields of a message in the event, not hex data in a module's parameter

options.text: Nothing about the cards, since the module's entries show only twelve digits of each account number
options.says: the translation entry shows twelve digits, but the MAC entry holds the whole packed request, card number included

origin.section: 7.3.1 Spot the Problem: The Module That Logged Everything

questions.stem: Terminals verify the MAC of every answer. The server signs answers in a plain TransactionParticipant placed right before SendResponse. A purchase is declined with 51 by a participant that builds a fresh answer from a few fields of the request, puts it in the Context and votes ABORTED. What does the terminal do with that 51?

options.text: It shows a decline, since field 39 is readable whether or not the answer carries a MAC
options.says: a terminal that checks MACs believes only an answer that verifies; an unsigned one could have been written by anyone

options.text: It shows a decline, since the signing participant signs every answer that is in the Context
options.says: after the abort vote only abort participants are asked; a plain participant never sees this answer

options.text: It treats the outcome as unknown, since the answer arrives with no MAC under the terminal's key
options.says: nothing signs the 51 on the abort path, so it carries no MAC under the terminal's key; the terminal reverses and raises a MAC alert

options.text: It treats the outcome as unknown, since the answer arrives with a MAC under another terminal's key
options.says: nothing signs the answer on the abort path, so it carries no MAC under any key, its own terminal's or another's

origin.section: 7.4 Every Response Is Signed, on the Abort Path Too

concepts: The key file holds keys only under the LMK, so it is harmless alone and reads PINs together with the LMK file.
With a logger, the security module and key store log PIN blocks, keys under the LMK and MAC input in hex that no log listener masks, so they are deployed without one.
